# Welcome

I am a Postdoctoral Scholar in the Division of Environmental Health, Department of Population and Public Health Sciences at the University of Southern California.

My research focuses on:

- Air pollution and climate-related exposures  
- Neighborhood and built environment impacts
- Transportation policy (Zero Emission Vehicle adoption)

## About Me

<img src="images/profile.jpg" width="180" class="profile">

I am an environmental epidemiologist with a Ph.D. in Population Health Sciences from Harvard University. My research integrates epidemiology, biostatistics, and environmental science to understand how environmental and contextual factors jointly shape population health. Using population-level data, I aim to generate real-world evidence that informs public health policy and supports healthier communities.


---

## Research Interests

- Environmental epidemiology  
- Climate and health, particularly extreme heat and air pollution in the interaction between outdoor and indoor environments  
- Policy-relevant and translational research  
- Causal inference methods for population health

## Others

I am a competitive swimmer (the slow kind). My favorite stroke is butterfly, but I would never swim a 200 fly unless my coach asks; and even then, I might still say no.

I currently swim with the Caltech Masters Swim Team and previously trained with Boston University Masters. While in Boston, I especially enjoyed swimming in Walden Pond.

Special thanks to Dr. Wilt, who inspired me to join a masters swimming group and introduced me to open-water swimming during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Swimming brings me a lot of joy (and occasional surprises). I met my husband at the pool when I noticed that he lapped me every 150 yards. That’s when I knew he was the one (just kidding…).

My passion for swimming has also led me to a small side project on longitudinal performance among masters swimmers.
